why_incomplete: D1 (confirmed by Tern): a failed SATURATED send is stamped as reported. In 4 of 5 runs duty was never told while the backlog lasted, and the log claimed 'duty told'. The SATURATED obligation is met only in crash-3, where the transport did not fail.

D2 (Tern: the 150 ms sleep is not closure): a yield does not hand off the lock. run re-acquired in the same millisecond at all 3 observed yields; waiting writers got in only after a non-yielding run pass. The reverse also happens: in drain-1 (2x overload) run had no hold for 114 s. So competing-writer progress AT the yield boundary is not shown, and supervisor freshness is not bounded.

D3 (new, found in crash-3): a settlement notice in flight when its holder is SIGKILLed is delivered twice. The next holder (24 ms later) re-settles from the marker and re-sends it. The ledger keeps one settlement, but the effect is duplicated, so 'no duplicate effect' fails.

b_local_time.result: local time inside a hold = hold minus the union of the holder's own stub wake intervals. It includes fork/exec, SQLite, file I/O and CPU. Max 0.104 s over 425 holds in 5 runs (p95 at most 0.095 s). Host: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 threads, kernel 7.0.14, overlay on the root disk; 2 runs were concurrent in pairs. Empirical for this host and load, not a bound on storage stalls. No outliers suppressed.

proposal_for_D2.mechanism: A lock hand-off registry beside the flock (no daemon). A waiter registers <db>.waiters/<seq>-<pid>-<starttime> when it starts waiting, and removes it when it gets the lock or gives up. A holder that is about to take the lock AGAIN (run after a yield or a pass), or any new arrival, first yields to the oldest LIVE registered waiter: it waits until that entry is gone. An entry whose pid is dead or reused (start time differs) is removed by whoever sees it, so a crashed waiter cannot block. Deadline callbacks and run register with priority 'due/run', ordinary dispatch with 'ordinary'. The oldest priority entry goes first, and an ordinary arrival never jumps ahead of a registered run or callback.
proposal_for_D2.bounds: Each hold is <= 10.5 s (existing budget). A registered waiter gets the lock within (entries ahead) x 10.5 s. Ordinary waiters already give up at 60 s, so at most ceil(60/5) ordinary entries exist at the supported arrival rate. run's gap is then <= (callbacks + 1) x 10.5 s under the supported model, not 114 s. The queue is bounded by the existing 60 s give-up and by dead-entry removal, so it cannot grow without limit.
proposal_for_D2.supported_contention_model: <= 1 ordinary arrival per 5 s, <= 14 due deadlines at one instant, 1 run, the liveness check. Above that, arrivals are refused (visible E_LEDGER_BUSY), as now.
proposal_for_D2.D1_fix: Stamp only on wake rc 0/3; a failed report is retried by the next holder. Tests: rc1, runner error, rc0/3, budget refusal, restart.
proposal_for_D2.D3_fix: Record the notice attempt under the lock before the wake. A replay that finds an attempt without a receipt re-sends once, marked 'REPEAT of <id>: delivery unknown after a crash'. Bounded to one visible repeat per crash, never silent.
proposal_for_D2.sizing: Author 75 min (registry and hand-off 40, D1 10, D3 25, with unit and mutation tests) + independent evidence 45 min (this harness rerun plus a crashed-waiter case and a 2x-overload freshness case) + review 30 min = 150 min. Not started; needs a new grant.
